Stated Claim / Post Context:
Hayden Panettiere’s Death Ruled Accidental

Her death was ruled accidental

Actual Article Body:
Photo by Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images

Police in South Carolina deemed the death of Hayden Panettiere accidental and officially closed the case.

Greenville Police Department officials came to the conclusion that there was no foul play involved in the star’s death after conducting an investigation and assessing the medical examiner’s findings, according to KGET News.

A post shared by Hayden Panettiere (@haydenpanettiere)

The “Nashville” star was found unresponsive August 16 in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road.

Brian Hickerson, Panettiere’s on-and-off boyfriend, and his brother, Zach Hickerson, were at the residence at the time of her passing, and a call was placed to 911 for medical assistance.

First responders rushed to the scene and attempted life-saving measures, but despite their best efforts, the famous actress was pronounced dead at 2:32 pm, according to WYFF 4.

A post shared by Momé (@dear.mome)

Panettiere’s former boyfriend provided medics with a bag of medications she was believed to have been taking prior to her death. Prior to her passing, Panettiere released a memoir detailing alleged abuse within their relationship.

The Greenville County Coroner’s Office determined the star died from an accidental overdose of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, methocarbamol, and Quetiapine, according to KGET News. (RELATED: Man Charged In Death Of Monaco Royal Family Member Antoine De Massy)

A post shared by Hayden Panettiere (@haydenpanettiere)

Panettiere’s sudden death at just 36 sent shockwaves through the entertainment industry, prompting an outpouring of heartfelt tributes from fans and colleagues who took to social media to mourn the beloved star and bid her a final farewell.
